- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above recent high for next 5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.20) within 5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; reduce forecast by 3–7% for 30d horizon.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast if recent 7d average is below 70.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3 days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize trend continuation; adjust forecast to match 3-day moving average.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.05) and price is near support, model tends to underestimate; add 1–4% upward bias if price is below 70.5.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day highs; if forecast exceeds 75.0 for 3 consecutive days, reduce by 5–10% for next 7 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
